title: Hom into a K-injective complex computes localized derived morphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$; write $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O|_U$ for the restriction to the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ and $Q_U$ for the localization functor from cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules to the derived category $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal L^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and $\mathcal I^\bullet$ a K-injective complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. A degree-$0$ cocycle of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is a morphism of complexes $f:\mathcal L^\bullet|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$, and the map
$$
 H^0\bigl(\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet))\bigr)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}\bigl(Q_U(\mathcal L^\bullet|_U),Q_U(\mathcal I^\bullet|_U)\bigr),\qquad [f]\longmapsto Q_U(f),
$$
is well defined and bijective.

proof.text: For sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules, restriction to $\mathcal C/U$ and extension by zero are obtained from the corresponding abelian-sheaf functors by carrying the $\mathcal O$-action along restriction and extension. The adjunction and exactness therefore hold in the module categories by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with restriction as the right adjoint and extension by zero as the exact left adjoint. Therefore $\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is K-injective on $\mathcal C/U$.

source.place: Lemma 0A94, reduction to the localized site and K-injective target

proof.text: By the definition of the sheaf-valued Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], a degree-$0$ global cocycle is exactly a chain map $f:\mathcal L^\bullet|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$, and a degree-$0$ coboundary is exactly a null-homotopy. Hence $H^0(\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)))$ is canonically $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O_U)}(\mathcal L^\bullet|_U,\mathcal I^\bullet|_U)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A94, identification of degree-zero Hom-complex cohomology

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] in the abelian category of $\mathcal O_U$-modules to the complex $\mathcal L^\bullet|_U$ and the K-injective target $\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ from Step 1. It gives a bijection from the homotopy-category morphisms to $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(Q_U(\mathcal L^\bullet|_U),Q_U(\mathcal I^\bullet|_U))$, induced by $f\mapsto Q_U(f)$. Combining this with Step 2 proves that the displayed map is well defined and bijective.
